THE PROBLEM
The page shows everything a task KNOWS while the keeper is trying to DO a chore.

Recurrence rules, streaks, enclosure and animal names, full dates — all at 10px, on every row, above three filter rows that consume roughly 15% of the screen before a single task appears.

A — THE DOING LIST

One scope row instead of three. Overdue pinned above the day. Rows carry a title and one context line; recurrence and streak move to editing. Swipe right to complete, with an Undo toast replacing the silent "All Done".

Tradeoff: incremental. It fixes this page rather than questioning whether one page should do both jobs.

B — DO / MANAGE SPLIT

Two tabs. "To do" is a short, almost chrome-free list you work through. "Schedules" is where recurrence rules and streaks live, because there they are the point.

Tradeoff: a keeper who wants to tweak a schedule mid-chore now has to switch tabs. Costs a tap to save a lot of density.

C — DAY RAIL

Today laid out on a time rail with a NOW marker, so you see the shape of the day: where work clusters, what is already behind, how much of the evening is committed.

Tradeoff: only works for a single day, and it wastes vertical space when someone has three tasks. Weak for the "All Tasks" view.
